newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Friday were quiet after this week's active sales, feedlot sources said.

Rain, snow and record-breaking low temperatures in the Texas Panhandle, combined with strong wind, made for miserable, sloppy conditions, they said. Cattle were bunching against the wind and ignoring feed bunks to some extent.
Weather Services Corp meteorologists forecast one to two more inches of rain in the Amarillo area after an overnight snowfall left about an inch of accumulation on the ground.
Kansas sources said their lots were largely unscathed.
WSC said light showers fell in southern Kansas with about 0.25 inch in southeast areas and 0.1 to 0.5 inch in southwest and northeast Kansas.
Fed cattle prices next week were seen trading at $67.00 per cwt, unchanged from light sales on Thursday but down $1.00 from this week's top prices.
The bulk of this week's cattle sold at $68.00, but declines in beef prices amid heavy slaughter pushed packer bids lower, cattle feeders said.
But the lower beef prices ignited hefty beef sales, sources noted.

The brisk beef movement could support cattle prices once packers work through large numbers of cattle they bought the last two weeks, sources noted. If beef demand remains strong, it could offset potential price weakness from expected increases in cattle supplies.
